review_coverage.assessment: AuthoritativeStateLedger in authoritative_state_ledger_v2.py inherits core transaction, idempotency, versioning, crash rollback/recovery, outbox, and concurrency mechanisms from v1 without regression.

authoritative_state_ledger_v2.py audit() reconstructs command_digest from persisted command_type, payload_json, expected_version, project_id, idempotency_key, effect_type, and effect_payload_json, detecting payload or effect tampering.

authoritative_state_ledger_v2.py audit() recomputes state_digest for current project_state, replays event transitions to verify result states, and checks current state consistency against event replay lineage.

test_slice5_authoritative_state_ledger_v2.py extends S5-16 to independently attack stored command payload, current project state, outbox effect payload, and deleted event lineage, confirming fail-closed detection across all attack vectors.
Authority claims provided by worker/model outputs in apply_command and complete_outbox are explicitly rejected (AuthorityClaimRejected), and outbox completion evidence rebinding fails closed.

The frozen contract and implementation clearly acknowledge bounded nonclaims: local SQLite single-database reference only, no distributed consensus, no multi-host atomicity, no cryptographic tamper-proofing, and no production durability guarantees.
Slice 4 regression suite runs cleanly (16/16 tests) alongside Slice 5, and the candidate adds no deployment, tool dispatch, release, or merge authority.
CI run 34229441085 is bound to candidate commit d9459af74533fbb60477dfcec00b30e82a0e2534 and completed successfully with 16/16 Slice 5 tests and 16/16 Slice 4 regression tests.

Adversarial inspection of authoritative_state_ledger_v2.py confirms that command digest reconstruction, state digest verification, replay lineage reconciliation, outbox integrity checks, and version continuity checks leave no material false-green paths within the single-database SQLite reference boundary.
